summary: The note describes how schools are partnering with local businesses and community groups to deliver practical, skills-oriented education, centered on Maplewood High School's partnerships launched in September 2023. It covers business collaborations, community programs, the changing role of teachers, an evaluation tool, and outcomes such as higher engagement and enrollment. Other schools like Falcon Crest Academy are replicating the model, and the outlook for a skilled workforce is optimistic.
one_line: Schools like Maplewood High are partnering with local businesses and community groups to deliver skills-based education, with measurable gains in engagement and enrollment.
key_facts: Maplewood High School announced its first school-business partnership on September 15, 2023, led by Principal Katherine Johnston.
Maplewood partnered with local businesses Tech Innovations Inc. and GreenLeaf Sustainability Co. to offer internships, mentorships, and project-based learning.
Tech Innovations Inc. offers coding workshops and apprenticeships for students interested in software development.
GreenLeaf Sustainability Co. lets students collaborate on environmental projects, embedding sustainable practices into learning.
Ted Mitchell, CEO of Tech Innovations Inc., said in an October 3, 2023 interview: "We're investing in the community and the workforce of tomorrow."

The Heartwood Community Center, led by Director Michael Rodriguez, began integrating social services and cultural programs into school life in November 2023, including food security drives with the local Food Bank.
Emily Thompson, an engineering teacher, said on January 12, 2024 that she is now a "collaborator and co-learner" working on engineering problems from business partners.

Jonathan Hales, an educational researcher, designed a bespoke evaluation tool released on February 25, 2024 that measures learning depth and economic impact, including student self-confidence and community well-being.
By the end of the 2023-2024 academic year, Maplewood reported a 12% increase in student engagement and 15% more students enrolling in vocational and apprenticeship programs.
Falcon Crest Academy formed alliances with agro-based enterprises, and Principal Anna Lawrence said on March 5, 2024 that agricultural program enrollment rose by 20%.
Teachers have shifted from traditional instruction to roles as project managers and advisors.
Schools evaluate partnerships using mixed methods combining qualitative feedback with quantitative engagement and achievement data.
